title: Cresta Alternatives for B2B Sales Teams
summary: Five honest Cresta alternatives for B2B sales teams, from meeting-native copilots to dialler platforms, with a comparison table and buying advice.
body_markdown:
Cresta is one of the strongest real-time agent-assist platforms on the market, and it is still the wrong tool for most B2B sales teams. This guide covers the best Cresta alternatives for teams that sell in scheduled video meetings rather than on contact-centre phone lines.


## 01


Why do B2B sales teams look for Cresta alternatives?


First, a definition. Real-time agent assist is software that listens to a live conversation and shows the person on the call useful guidance while they speak: suggested answers, objection responses, prompts, and checklists. Cresta helped define the category and does it well.


But Cresta is built for the contact centre. That means telephony at the core, thousands of short calls a day, supervisor dashboards, automated QA scoring, and an enterprise deployment that involves IT, security review, and integration work with your phone stack. For a support organisation or a high-volume inside sales floor, all of that is the point.


B2B selling looks different. Deals run for weeks or months across a handful of scheduled video calls on Zoom, Meet, or Teams. The knowledge a rep needs mid-call is deal-specific: what the security doc says, what the champion promised last week, how a similar customer handled the same objection. That knowledge lives in your docs, CRM, and past calls, and a script-and-compliance engine tuned for call centres has no natural place to hold it. Teams leave Cresta over fit, not quality. Paying contact-centre procurement weight for ten meetings a week per rep is the usual last straw.


## 02


What is Cresta actually good at?


Credit where it is due. Cresta delivers live guidance on phone calls at serious scale, scores every conversation for QA without humans listening to samples, gives supervisors a real-time view of the floor, and surfaces what top performers do differently. If you run a large inside sales or customer service operation on a telephony platform, Cresta belongs on your shortlist and you probably should not switch. This article is for the teams whose selling happens somewhere else.


## 03


The 5 best Cresta alternatives for B2B sales teams


### 1. Caretta


Our own product, so weigh the bias accordingly. It is a real-time copilot built for the scheduled B2B sales meeting rather than the phone queue. It joins live video calls and answers the hard moments as they happen: a pricing objection, a security question, a competitor mention. The difference is where the answers come from. It learns from your docs, CRM, past calls, and your best reps, so the guidance is specific to the deal on screen instead of a generic script. Deployment is light enough for a sales team to own, without a contact-centre platform purchase; the[product page](https://www.caretta.so/product) shows how the pieces fit. The honest caveat: if your team lives in a dialler and makes two hundred calls a day, a meeting-native copilot is the wrong shape for you too.


### 2. Clari Copilot


Clari Copilot (formerly Wingman) is the conversation intelligence arm of the Clari revenue platform. It records and analyses meetings, and it offers real-time battle cards triggered by keywords, so a competitor mention can pop the right talking points. Its real strength is context: calls sit next to pipeline data, forecasts, and deal health inside Clari. If your organisation already runs Clari, Copilot is the low-friction choice. The real-time layer is thinner than Cresta's, though; it is keyword-triggered cards rather than deep live assistance, and most of the value lands after the call. The tradeoff between those two modes is worth understanding before you buy; we cover it in[conversation intelligence vs real-time call guidance](https://www.caretta.so/blog/conversation-intelligence-vs-real-time) .


### 3. Dialpad


Dialpad is the closest like-for-like Cresta alternative on this list, because it is also contact-centre-flavoured: it owns the phone system and layers Ai Agent Assist cards, live transcription, and coaching on top. That makes it the better Cresta alternative in one specific case: a phone-heavy inside sales team that wants telephony and AI assist from a single vendor, with a lighter purchase than a standalone enterprise agent-assist platform bolted onto someone else's phones. Be clear-eyed about what it does not solve. If your objection to Cresta is the contact-centre shape itself, Dialpad has the same shape, and its meeting-side assistance is not the core of the product.


### 4. Outreach Kaia


Kaia is the real-time meeting assistant inside the Outreach sales engagement platform. It joins video meetings, transcribes live, surfaces content cards when buyers ask about topics you have prepared, and pushes action items back into Outreach workflows. For teams that already run their sequences and pipeline in Outreach, Kaia is a sensible way to get live assistance without a new vendor. Outside that ecosystem it is a hard sell: you are buying a sales engagement platform to get the assistant, and the guidance leans on content you set up in advance rather than on your wider knowledge base.


### 5. Nooks


Nooks covers the case the meeting-native tools ignore: dialler-heavy SDR teams. It is an AI-powered parallel dialler with a virtual sales floor, call recording, and AI feedback on cold calls. If your SDRs measure their day in dials and connects, Nooks attacks the real bottleneck, which is connect volume and fast coaching loops, and it does so with far less deployment weight than a contact-centre platform. It is not a tool for demos or late-stage deal calls, and it does not try to be. Pair it with a meeting-focused assistant if your team does both motions.


## 04


How do the Cresta alternatives compare?


Tool Built for Real-time assistance Knowledge source Procurement weight


**Caretta** Scheduled B2B video meetings Deep, deal-specific answers live Your docs, CRM, past calls, top reps Light, sales-team owned


**Clari Copilot** Revenue teams on Clari Keyword-triggered battle cards Cards and content you configure Medium, part of Clari


**Dialpad** Phone-heavy teams wanting one vendor Assist cards on calls it hosts Configured playbooks and FAQs Medium, replaces your phone system


**Outreach Kaia** Teams already on Outreach Content cards in meetings Prepared Outreach content Heavy unless you own Outreach


**Nooks** Dialler-heavy SDR teams Coaching and feedback on cold calls Call recordings and scorecards Light for what it does


## 05


Which Cresta alternative should you choose?


Start from where your revenue conversations happen, then pick the tool shaped for that place.


1. **Scheduled video meetings with long deal cycles:** choose a meeting-native copilot that draws on your own deal knowledge.
2. **Already standardised on Clari or Outreach:** try the assistant you already half-own, Copilot or Kaia, before adding a vendor.
3. **Phone-heavy inside sales wanting one bill:** Dialpad, and accept that you are buying a phone system first.
4. **SDR cold-calling at volume:** Nooks, and solve meetings separately.
5. **A true contact centre:** stay with Cresta and stop reading listicles.
